2607.00990.title: SWE-Doctor: Guiding Software Engineering Agents with Runtime Diagnosis from Multi-Faceted Bug Reproduction Tests
2607.00990.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM)-based software engineering agents are increasingly developed to resolve software issues by generating patches from issue reports and code repositories. Bug reproduction tests (BRTs) are an important building block for such agents and have been shown useful for patch validation. However, it remains unclear whether BRTs can also help the more central stage of patch generation. We first conduct a preliminary study and find that directly using advanced BRT generators to guide patch generation is not beneficial: fail-to-fail BRTs can mislead agents, while even fail-to-pass BRTs bring limited or negative gains. Our analysis reveals two reasons: fail-to-pass BRTs may cover only one manifestation of the reported issue, leading to partial patches, whereas fail-to-fail BRTs are unreliable as direct patch-generation targets. Motivated by these insights, we propose SWE-Doctor, a software issue resolution agent that guides patch generation with runtime diagnoses derived from multi-faceted BRT executions. SWE-Doctor first generates multi-faceted BRTs for different behavioral requirements stated in the issue, then executes and debugs these BRTs to construct runtime-grounded diagnosis records, and finally uses the diagnoses together with localization information inferred during BRT generation to guide patch generation and reduce partial patches. We evaluate SWE-Doctor on Python bug-fixing issues from the widely adopted SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Pro across five LLM backends. SWE-Doctor consistently outperforms existing agents across all 10 LLM-benchmark combinations, achieving average resolution rates of 75.7% on SWE-bench Verified and 59.4% on SWE-bench Pro. In particular, on the more challenging SWE-bench Pro, SWE-Doctor improves the average resolution rate by 8.0-8.9 percentage points over the baseline agents.
2607.00990.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）為基礎的軟體工程代理正在不斷開發，以通過從問題報告和代碼庫生成修補程式來解決軟體問題。<lb/>錯誤重現測試（BRTs）是這些代理的重要基石，並已被證明對修補程式驗證有用。<lb/>然而，目前尚不清楚BRTs是否也能幫助修補程式生成的更核心階段。<lb/>我們首先進行了一項初步研究，發現直接使用先進的BRT生成器來指導修補程式生成並沒有好處：失敗到失敗的BRTs可能會誤導代理，而即使是失敗到通過的BRTs也帶來有限或負面的收益。<lb/>我們的分析揭示了兩個原因：失敗到通過的BRTs可能僅涵蓋報告問題的一種表現，導致部分修補程式，而失敗到失敗的BRTs作為直接修補程式生成目標則不可靠。<lb/>受到這些見解的啟發，我們提出了SWE-Doctor，一個通過從多面向BRT執行中獲得的運行時診斷來指導修補程式生成的軟體問題解決代理。<lb/>SWE-Doctor首先為問題中陳述的不同行為需求生成多面向的BRTs，然後執行和調試這些BRTs以構建運行時基礎的診斷記錄，最後使用這些診斷以及在BRT生成過程中推斷的定位信息來指導修補程式生成並減少部分修補程式。<lb/>我們在來自廣泛採用的SWE-bench Verified和SWE-bench Pro的Python錯誤修復問題上評估了SWE-Doctor，涵蓋五個LLM後端。<lb/>SWE-Doctor在所有10個LLM基準組合中穩定超越現有代理，在SWE-bench Verified上實現了75.7%的平均解決率，在SWE-bench Pro上實現了59.4%的平均解決率。<lb/>特別是在更具挑戰性的SWE-bench Pro上，SWE-Doctor將平均解決率提高了8.0-8.9個百分點，相較於基線代理。
